topic: Phone screen black after water: telling a failed display from a dead phone
record_type: Draft on branch claude/project-thread-1qrr7r; not published until the owner says yes in chat
uniqueness: 73-guide inventory checked. Nearest pages: water-damaged-phone (general first-five-minutes triage for any wet phone), phone-screen-black-but-on (black screen mostly after a drop, one forced restart), iphone-liquid-detected-port-dry and iphone-speaker-muffled-after-water. None covers a black screen after liquid as its own symptom. This page leads with the owner's bench point, skips the restart and charge steps for a wet phone, and links both nearest pages instead of repeating them. Queue item 5, requested by the owner on Nov 15.
bench_point: Owner, Nov 15 (paraphrased on the page, no percentage printed): he gets these jobs constantly, and on iPhones the phone usually just needs a new display, as long as it wasn't left sitting wet for a long time.
scope: A phone whose screen went fully black after liquid exposure. Black screens after a dry drop, and screens with lines or patches, are routed to other guides.

sources.retrieval: Read. Unplug; tap gently with connector facing down; dry area with airflow; at least 30 minutes before trying a cable; up to 24 hours to dry; no external heat or compressed air; no cotton swab or paper towel in the connector; no rice (particles can damage the phone); charging while wet can corrode pins and cause permanent damage.

Read. Resistance is not permanent and can decrease with normal wear; liquid damage not covered under warranty; don't charge until completely dry; allow at least 5 hours before charging with a Lightning or USB-C cable or connecting an accessory.
Read. Liquid damage service not covered by the Apple One-Year Limited Warranty; Liquid Contact Indicators.
Read. Black screen steps: forced restart, then charge for an hour. Cited to explain why those steps don't fit a wet phone.

Read. Device appears in the Finder sidebar on macOS Catalina or later; Apple Devices app on Windows. iTunes is named on the page from the owner's own wording for older Windows setups, not from this source.
